messages:
sarah.k: Hey team, customer reported inconsistent embedding lengths across our environments. Hosted returns 1536 vectors, but Dedicated and Private sometimes return 1534 or 1537. This started after the recent routing/quantization change.

amal: ugh, that's bad for their k-NN index. Do we have a request id or sample payload?

sarah.k: Request id: r-8f2c2b. Sample input (short text) attached below. They hit embeddings endpoint via SDK + automatic batching.

support-qa: Repro'd locally on a staging Dedicated cluster — observed vector length flipping when batch_size > 8 and payloads include an empty string.

henry_r: Interesting — empty strings could be tripping padding logic in the C++ batcher. Can you paste the client payload and headers?

sarah.k: payload: `{ "input": ["hello world", "", "what is ML" ] }`

henry_r: Also check whether the client sets `preserve_length=true` or any legacy `pad_to` tweak. If pad_to==auto we used to infer shape from first non-empty which leads to races.

support-qa: Minimal repro curl:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-alpha-1","input":["hello","","hey"]}'
```

amal: On Hosted the inference runtime does extra normalization that strips empties before batching. Dedicated/private runtime currently preserves entries and relies on pad behavior — mismatch there explains parity.

henry_r: I filed an issue: GH #infra/1384. Root cause hypothesis: our batching path uses two different pad strategies depending on runtime flag `trim_empty_inputs`. Hosted had it enabled by default, Dedicated not.

ops-bot: deploy noticed: rolled back quantization kernel on hosted at 2025-09-12T18:01:22Z due to perf regression.

support-qa: Quick mitigation: client-side workaround is to filter empty strings before sending. Also setting `pad_to=1536` explicitly normalizes shape across envs.

amal: Can we add a short-term server-side guard that treats empty input as zero-vector instead of dropping? That would be backwards-compatible.

henry_r: I'll push a small change to the Dedicated runtime to enable `trim_empty_inputs` for parity; that'll be a config toggle and a patch on the batcher. Rolling to canary now.

sarah.k: Customer update sent: asked them to disable batching and strip empties while we patch. They appreciated the workaround but want a timeline.

henry_r: ETA: canary in 2 hours, full rollout overnight if no regressions. I'll attach the PR once ready.

support-qa: Tests to run before rollout: (1) batch sizes 1..64, (2) with/without empty strings, (3) onpad/pad_to behaviour, (4) embedding dimension assert in response. We'll add a unit check that response.vector.length == model.dim.

amal: Also add an observability alert when more than 0.1% of responses deviate from expected dim for a model across any region.

sarah.k: filing a follow-up ticket with account billing note — customer requested a credit for noisy results last week.

ops-bot: ticket created: SUPPORT-4839 assigned to sarah.k

henry_r: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/862 (toggle + tests). Canary link: https://canary.redwood.ai/dedicated/patch-862

support-qa: Confirmed canary returns stable 1536 vectors for all tested payloads including empty strings. No latency regression observed at 99th p95.

amal: great. Let's track and close after 24h of canary traffic.

sarah.k: thanks all — I'll follow up after canary window and reconcile billing request. :thumbsup:
